mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the previous three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.5% mean) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) during episodes where GDPC1 falls >2% YoY and UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and boosts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +50,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.5% mean) during periods of four consecutive months of >50,000 increase in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.7% mean) during three consecutive months of INDPRO decline > -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in demand, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.2% mean) when GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > -1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL < 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.8% mean) when FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 months and CPIAUCSL < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a very tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.6% mean) when UNRATE < 3.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 2% for three consecutive months, coincident with a flat or declining GDPC1, signals a shift from consumption to saving and weak aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +2% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 not rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5% mean) when RSAFS rises >2% for three months and GDPC1 is flat or falling.
